scope: Proposed classification and focused-introduction mapping for 19 unchanged exercises: 15 N4 temporal exercises and four N3 expectation/obligation exercises. No runtime fields or manifest changes are made in phase A. Other exercises remain unclassified and available through the documented compatibility path.

classifications.rationale: The controlled contrast requires both before and after relations, including the relative-time verb attachment and noun patterns. JLPT Sensei places mae ni at N5 but ato de at N4; label the complete contrast N4 rather than its easier target alone. Extending the after-family classification to the supplied ato ni frames is editorial judgment, not a claim that the source labels those exact sentences or particle choices. Existing grammar-before-after-sources.json documents the ni/de qualification.
classifications.limits: Not a claim that every isolated mae/no-ato expression is N4, that the prompt uses only N4 vocabulary, or that optional spelling variants each require separate study.

classifications.rationale: Bunpro explicitly places the about-to and just-completed tokoro lessons at N4. The Japan Foundation's BMA00036 covers the complete dictionary/teiru/ta three-stage contrast used here, with an old level-3 label. The modern N4 classification of the complete group is a corroborated editorial choice, not a mechanical conversion of an old JLPT label.
classifications.limits: Controlled verb-form selection before printed tokoro does not establish unrestricted selection among tokoro, bakari, tsumori or every stative/resultative teiru use.

classifications.rationale: Bunpro places hazu da at N4 and beki at N3. These four questions explicitly contrast expectation with obligation/advisability, so N3 describes the required contrast, including questions whose answer is hazu. Other koto/wake functions in the same file are not classified by this record.
classifications.limits: Do not adopt the source's claim that beki always names the only permissible action, its kanji-based explanation, or a universal strength rule. Existing exercise meanings and accepted answers are unchanged.

next.reason: Extend relative before/after timing to distinguishing immediately before, during and just after one action.

authoringNotes: All 401 runtime exercise records, article text, accepted answers, exercise IDs and the manifest remain unchanged in phase A.
The classifications are single proposed levels per exercise, not redundant N3/N2/N1 tags. Level membership is derived in the application.
The complete paired contrast determines the level; the easier model answer alone does not. Optional spelling/contraction acceptance is not a second learning item.
Example keys keep reused lexical contexts visible without counting repeated versions as independent context coverage within a facet.

The temporal recommendation is an editorial connection between related topics, not a source-attested prerequisite, equivalence of mae/ato and tokoro, proven transfer effect or requirement to finish one before the other.
No true prerequisites are authored. Their malformed/cyclic/missing-reference behavior belongs in synthetic implementation fixtures, not invented linguistic dependencies.
The other four koto/wake exercises in the pilot file remain unclassified and ungrouped. No broad level is inferred from that file's title or article.
N5 is intentionally empty in this classified subset. N2/N1 scopes include the classified N4/N3 exercises but no N2/N1 mastery or coverage is claimed.
The 404 guessed Bunpro URLs for mae ni and ta ato de and an unsuccessful broad web search were not evidence. Actual discovered URLs and HTML headings were inspected.

Independent review must assess classifications/grouping and the contract; the existing examples are unchanged, and this does not establish native-speaker validation, corpus frequency or learning effectiveness.
